---
title: "Automorphic Equivalence"
---

## Introduction

Beyond structural equivalence, network analysts also study a deeper structural concept called **automorphic equivalence**. Two actors are automorphically equivalent if they occupy indistinguishable structural locations in the overall network, even if their specific neighbors are entirely different people.

## Structural Isomorphism

Think of it in terms of structural symmetry: if you can swap the identities (labels) of two actors (and possibly their neighbors) and the overall structure of the graph remains mathematically identical, they are automorphically equivalent. This is a very strict definition of being in the "same structural position."
